item.title: Clover Health: Chairman Programs Lead
item.description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

Own the white space. Operate with autonomy. Drive the programs that move the company.

We’re hiring a high-agency operator into the Office of the Chairman to drive Clover’s most important cross-functional initiatives from ambiguity to execution and results.

This is a rare role designed for someone who thrives at the intersection of strategy, systems design, and executional rigor. You’ll operate as a force-multiplier to the Chairman and executive team: orchestrating execution across organizational boundaries, defining innovative pilots, testing hypotheses, structuring problems that don’t yet have owners, and driving initiatives that directly shape Clover’s growth and operational leverage.

As a Chairman Programs Lead, you will:

  • Architect Strategic Programs: Translate high-level goals into MECE workstreams with clear interfaces, owners, and timelines.
  • Drive Execution with Chairman-Standard Rigor: Own initiatives from kickoff through outcomes. Set the pace. Maintain altitude and detail without losing either.
  • Align Stakeholders Across Levels and Functions: Influence without authority. Drive accountability through clarity, not escalation.
  • Translate Ambiguity Into Action: When no playbook exists, build one. When priorities are unclear, force rank them. When coordination breaks down, rebuild the system.
  • Collaborate Across Boundaries: Manage projects that touch internal teams and external partners — vendors, regulators, and strategic collaborators. Align internal readiness to external dependencies.

Success in this role looks like:

  • First 90 days: Quickly grasp Clover's business model, establish key relationships, identify 2-3 high-priority initiatives, and implement a structured framework for tracking strategic projects.
  • First 6 months: Successfully drive multiple cross-functional initiatives to completion, develop systems improving operational efficiency, and establish yourself as a trusted Chairman advisor on strategic priorities.
  • First year: Create scalable coordination mechanisms that improve execution across teams, resolve strategic misalignments, and deliver measurable business impact on growth and operational leverage.

You should get in touch if:

  • You’ve had 3–10 years of experience at a top-tier consulting firm (e.g., McKinsey, Bain, BCG), in BizOps at a tech company, or in a high-trust internal strategy/Chief of Staff-type role. 
  • You think in structured logic, write with precision, and speak in synthesized insights.
  • You’re not a deck-maker. You’re a system builder who wants to see the impact of your thinking play out in operations.
  • You’ve driven complex, multi-org initiatives to the finish line — not just advised on them.
  • You’re energized by ambiguity, allergic to bureaucracy, and motivated by direct proximity to decision-making and value creation.
  • You don’t need positional authority to lead. You earn trust and create alignment through clarity, quality, and velocity.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities
  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Chief Actuary

Remote - USA

The Finance team at Clover Health is a group of strategic partners providing financial and operational insights that drive informed decision-making and efficient capital allocation. Guided by our core values of excellence, accountability, and collaboration, we provide actionable recommendations to improve health outcomes and reduce costs while ensuring financial integrity and innovation.

Actuarial is at the center of some of Clover's most important decisions—from pricing and forecasting to reserving, medical economics, and long-term strategy. As Chief Actuary, you'll lead and evolve this function during a pivotal stage of the company's growth, helping shape how we deploy AI, automation, and advanced analytics to improve decision-making across the business.

This isn't a traditional Chief Actuary role. We're looking for someone who can combine deep actuarial expertise with modern technology, building AI-enabled workflows that transform how actuarial work gets done while maintaining the rigor, transparency, and governance required in a highly regulated environment. You'll partner closely with leaders across Finance, Clinical, Growth, Operations, and Product to influence company strategy while building a best-in-class actuarial organization.

  • Guide reserving methodology, IBNR development, forecasting, and emerging experience analysis to provide timely, reliable financial insights.

  • Gain deep familiarity with Clover's pricing, forecasting, reserving, and medical economics processes.

  • Begin implementing AI-enabled actuarial workflows that improve efficiency and insight generation.

item.title: Faire: Director, Global Equity
item.description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Faire is revolutionizing wholesale and helping local retailers and their suppliers succeed in a technology-enabled era. As a Director, Global Equity, you will own and continue to evolve Faire’s global equity programs, building on an existing foundation while enhancing the structure, rigor, and scalability required to support public company readiness. This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, brings strong judgment, and wants to shape how equity operates with true end-to-end ownership.

As a Director, Global Equity You Will

  • Own and scale Faire’s global equity programs end-to-end, spanning plan design, administration, accounting, compliance, and employee experience across all equity award types and jurisdictions.
  • Serve as the senior owner of equity operations, partnering with Finance, Accounting, Payroll, Legal, and People to build durable, audit-ready processes that scale with company growth.
  • Lead public company equity responsibilities, including SEC reporting support, insider trading programs, audit readiness, and the design and operation of equity-related internal controls.
  • Oversee the full equity lifecycle, including grant issuance, vesting, exercises, releases, share pool management, and reconciliations between the equity platform and general ledger.
  • Design, implement, and optimize equity systems and workflows, including Shareworks (or equivalent) integrations with payroll, HRIS, and financial reporting systems.
  • Act as a trusted advisor and escalation point for complex employee, executive, and stakeholder equity matters, exercising sound judgment and discretion.
  • Proactively manage global regulatory, tax, and compliance risk, partnering with Legal and external advisors to ensure equity programs remain compliant as Faire scales internationally.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance, Accounting, Law or equivalent practical experience
  • 10+ years of experience in stock plan administration, including leadership in complex or high-growth environments
  • CEP certification strongly preferred
  • Deep expertise in global equity programs, with hands-on knowledge of legal, tax, and payroll considerations across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Experience with designing and implementing an Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Proven experience scaling equity programs through private-to-public readiness or public company operations.
  • Advanced analytical and systems skills; Shareworks (or equivalent) expertise required.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functionally without authority, including working with senior leaders.
  • You are resourceful and not afraid to roll up your sleeves.

Salary Range

California & New York: the pay range for this role is $184,000 to $253,000 per year.

Zone B: the pay range for this role is $165,500 to $227,500 per year.

Zone C: the pay range for this role is $147,000 to $202,500 per year.

Note: This is a remote role open to candidates located in Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, or Wisconsin

Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting. 

Why you’ll love working at Faire

  • Move fast: You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.
  • Equipped to scale: We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.
  • Best in class: Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.
  • Real rewards. Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.
  • Belonging: We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.

Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We are looking for a Chief of Staff–style operator to serve as the President’s right hand and help run, maintain, and continuously evolve the Product, Engineering & Design operating model and cadence. 

This role will turn strategy into a durable execution system. You will own the connective tissue across the President’s leadership cadence: preparing the right inputs, creating clarity on decisions and tradeoffs, ensuring commitments are followed through, surfacing risks early, and improving the operating model as the organization changes. You will work across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Finance, People, and your peers in Business Operations, partnering with senior leaders who do not report to you and influencing through judgment, trust, and clarity.

The successful candidate will combine executive judgment, operational rigor, business acumen, comfort with ambiguity, strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to move fluidly between strategic questions and the execution details required to make the system work. 

AI fluency is an important part of this role. You will use approved enterprise AI tools, including tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable platforms, to automate repeatable operating work, synthesize information across functions, improve leadership preparation, surface risks and dependencies, and accelerate strategic-initiative delivery.

This role reports to the VP of Operations at Squarespace and is based remotely in California or locally at our New York City headquarters. 

You’ll Get To… 

  • Run the President's operating cadence. Own end-to-end orchestration of the leadership rhythm: staff meetings, WBRs, MBRs, and QBRs, finance and portfolio reviews, priority updates, and annual operating-plan inputs. Ensure each ritual has a clear purpose, owner, input, output, decision authority, and downstream cascade.
  • Drive decision quality. Synthesize diverse inputs into concise narratives that make priorities, risks, options, tradeoffs, and recommended decisions clear to the President and leadership team. Document decisions in the room, assign owners and deadlines, track commitments, and escalate unresolved issues with context and a proposed path forward.
  • Improve execution velocity. Identify alignment and execution risks before they surface as leadership surprises, and facilitate resolution across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Customer Operations, Finance, People, and Business Operations, connecting planning, performance, financial, organizational, and roadmap inputs. item.description:
Headquarters: Tampa, Florida
URL: https://koast.ai

Head of Operations | Full-time | Remote (US hours) | Reports to the CEO | Growth path to VP of Operations / COO

Koast is the AI operating layer for teams that run Meta ads at volume. Agencies, in-house media buying teams, and enterprise buyers managing 10+ ad accounts and launching 50+ ads a week use Koast to launch faster, automate optimizations off real attribution data, and see every account from one Command Center. The Koast Agent is the next layer: an AI that reads the account, spots what matters, and acts inside guardrails.

We are bootstrapped, profitable, and growing faster than our processes. Customers are onboarding weekly through direct sales and partnerships, contractors span three time zones, and the CEO is still the person who notices when an invoice did not go out or a new customer never got their onboarding call. That stops with this hire.

You will be one of the first ten full-time employees at Koast. You will own how the company runs so the CEO can own where it goes. You are the anchor between engineering, support, customer success, and sales: the person who makes sure the vision the CEO sets actually gets executed, at a high standard, across every function.

This is not a back-office seat. You will live inside the product. You will know the launch flow, the Command Center, and the Agent well enough to run a customer onboarding yourself, reproduce a bug before you file it, and tell engineering which support ticket is a one-off and which one is a pattern.

What you will own

The anchor between functions. Sales promises something, engineering ships something, support hears about the gap. You sit in the middle of all four and close it. You will own the handoffs (sales to onboarding, support to engineering, engineering to customer success), make sure each team knows what the others are doing, and turn the CEO's priorities into a plan each function can execute this week.

The operating cadence. Weekly priorities, the metrics review, the state-of-the-union thread, the quarterly plan. You will build the rhythm the company runs on and make sure every function knows what it owes and when.

Revenue operations. The pipeline from lead to paid to renewed. GoHighLevel, Stripe, Granola, and the automations that tie them together. Clean data, accurate MRR and churn, a sales rep who never has to ask "where does this deal go."

Customer operations. Onboarding, support triage in Intercom, escalations, renewals, and the handoff from sales to success. Every enterprise account gets a named owner, a kickoff, and a 30-day check-in, and you will know which ones are at risk before they tell us.

People and contractors. Hiring pipelines, contractor agreements, onboarding docs, payroll and payouts, performance check-ins. As we go from a handful of contractors to a real team, you will build the system that makes each new person productive in their first week.

Finance operations. Bookkeeping hygiene, monthly close with our accountant, cash forecasting, vendor and tool spend, partner payouts (Whop, affiliates, referral partners). Not the CFO seat. The person who makes sure the numbers are right and the CEO sees them on the first of the month.

Partnerships and vendors. Contracts, renewals, compliance items (Meta platform terms, data policies), and the operational side of partnerships like Whop and Flex: who owes what, by when, and whether it happened.

Systems and automation. You will look at every recurring manual task and ask whether Zapier, an internal tool, or an AI agent should be doing it instead. Then you will build it or spec it for someone who can.

What you will do week to week

  • Run the weekly ops review: pipeline, churn, cash, hiring, blockers. One page, numbers first.
  • Use Koast every day. Run onboardings in it, triage support tickets against it, and bring engineering the patterns, not the anecdotes.
  • Translate the CEO's quarterly priorities into a plan with owners and dates across sales, support, success, and engineering, then hold each function to it.
  • Own the onboarding calendar for new customers and new hires so nothing waits on the CEO.
  • Keep the sales pipeline, CRM, and billing in sync and catch the exceptions before they become refund requests.
  • Draft and manage contractor agreements, vendor contracts, and partner order forms.
  • Close the books monthly with our bookkeeper and flag anything that looks wrong.
  • Build the automation or the SOP for any task you have done more than twice.
  • Write the updates: one for the CEO, one for the team, one for the partner. Each one short.
  • Say "we do not need this tool" and cancel it.

What sets you apart

  • You have been the operator behind a founder at a company that went from 5 to 50 people, or from $1M to $10M, and you built the systems that made that possible.
  • You know performance marketing or agency operations from the inside. You understand why a media buyer cares about a delayed ad account approval and what it costs when onboarding slips a week.
  • You are fluent in the modern ops stack (CRM, billing, bookkeeping, contracts, automation) and you configure it yourself rather than waiting on a consultant.
  • You are hands-on with software. You learn a product deeply, you can read a Shortcut ticket and a PostHog funnel, and engineers trust you to bring them a real problem instead of a forwarded complaint.
  • You have sat between sales, support, and engineering before and kept all three moving in the same direction without being the boss of any of them.
  • You bring numbers to every conversation and you are comfortable telling the CEO the number he does not want to hear.
  • You write tightly. Your SOPs are shorter than everyone else's and people actually follow them.
  • You are comfortable owning things nobody assigned you, and comfortable letting go of them when it is time to hire someone better.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in operations, revenue operations, or chief-of-staff roles at a B2B SaaS or agency, including at least one early-stage or high-growth environment.
  • Hands-on experience with a CRM (GoHighLevel, HubSpot, or similar), Stripe or comparable billing, and QuickBooks or comparable bookkeeping.
  • Experience managing contractors and vendors, including drafting and negotiating agreements.
  • Familiarity with Meta ads, agency workflows, or ad-tech is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience working directly with a software product and an engineering team: filing and prioritizing tickets, running QA or UAT, and using product analytics to make decisions.
  • Comfortable with Zapier, Make, or scripting light automations. Experience directing AI tools or agents to do operational work is a plus.
  • Available full-time during US business hours.

How You Work

Small team, high trust, no theater. Decisions are made with numbers, written down, and revisited when the numbers change. These are the values we run on. If they sound like you, you will fit right in.

  • Mastery. "Good enough" is where you start, not where you stop. You keep sharpening the craft: tighter systems, cleaner numbers, fewer surprises.
  • Push the Boundaries. You take on the ambitious version of the problem. Most ops teams manage the chaos. You want to build the company that does not have it.
  • Embrace the Challenge. When a customer's onboarding breaks at 9pm, you are in the thread, not waiting for the morning standup.
  • Responsibility. You own your commitments. If a date slips, everyone hears it from you first, with a new date attached.
  • Dedication. You dive into the hard, unglamorous problems (messy books, a broken handoff, a contract nobody read) and iterate until they are solved.
  • Collaboration. You write clearly, share what you learn, and make sales, engineering, and customers faster for having worked with you.

Why Koast

  • Early-stage impact. You will be one of the first ten full-time employees. How this company runs at 50 people will be the system you built at 10.
  • AI and ads at scale. You will operate at the frontier of AI-driven media buying, alongside some of the highest-volume ad teams on Meta.
  • Real upside. Bootstrapped and profitable, so the equity means something. Full-time salary, performance bonuses, paid time off, and a vested equity grant that grows with the seat as you move toward VP of Operations or COO.
  • Remote and flexible. Work from anywhere, on your schedule, during US hours. Just make sure the machine runs.

How to apply

Record a Loom, five minutes or less, covering these five things in order:

  1. Show us a system you built. Screen-share a process, dashboard, or automation you designed that the company still uses. Walk us through why it exists and what it replaced.
  2. One thing you would kill. A process, tool, or meeting you inherited and shut down, and what happened after.
  3. One number. A metric you owned, where it was when you started, where it was when you left, and what you changed.
  4. One handoff you fixed. A time sales, support, and engineering were not aligned, what it was costing, and how you closed the gap.
  5. Where Koast fits. Sixty seconds on what breaks first when a bootstrapped SaaS company doubles headcount, and what you would do in your first 30 days here to prevent it.

Email the Loom link and your LinkedIn or resume to jobs@koast.ai with the subject line "Scaling with Koast".

No cover letters. We watch the Loom first and read the resume second. Applications without the video are not reviewed.
